resource.name: Data sharing agreement 42 v3 rendered as a FHIR R5 Permission (output only, pre-adopted in R4)
resource.description:
A worked example of the one-way rendering of an ODRL 2.2 `Agreement` to a FHIR R5 `Permission`, pre-adopted in this FHIR R4 guide as a `Basic` with the R5 Permission cross-version extensions of `hl7.fhir.uv.xver-r5.r4` (each R5 element is the extension of the same name) (bean folio-assistant-jfbm; output only, the ODRL Agreement stays the source of truth). Ministry M shares its immunization coverage dataset with Institute I for public health use in 2026-2027, and may not have it redistributed.

Mapped: `conflict` prohibit to `combining` deny-overrides; `assigner` to `asserter`; the permission's `dateTime` constraints to `validity`; `uid` (the fixed-version URL) to `justification.evidence` as a logical reference; `permission` / `prohibition` to `rule.type` permit / deny; `target` to `rule.data.resource`; `assignee` to `rule.activity.actor`; `action` to `rule.activity.action` (consentaction); `purpose` to `rule.activity.purpose` (HL7 PurposeOfUse); the `delete` duty to `rule.limit` (v3 ObligationPolicy DELAU).

Dropped, with no home in Permission: the policy type `Agreement`; the agreement's SHA-256 (`spdx:checksum`; `Attachment.hash` is SHA-1 and `Reference` has no hash); the operator `isA` (only the code is kept); the exclusive bound of `lt` (Period end is inclusive, so the end is rendered as the last second before the bound); the `delete` duty's deadline constraint; the `inform` duty and its `informedParty`. Also without a home in Permission, though not used in this example: `refinement` on actions, assets or parties; the `elapsedTime` and other per-action constraints; `remedy` and `consequence`; logical constraints (`or`, `xone`, `and`, `andSequence`); `AssetCollection` / `PartyCollection` and `partOf`; `inheritFrom`; `profile`; `conflict` `invalid`; and duties other than those with an ObligationPolicy code (these map only roughly to `rule.limit`).

resource.description: No act of Lina's: implied consent with an opportunity to dissent (HL7 ActConsentDirective IMPLIEDD) under the example trust domain's default policy, the IHE PCF implicit policy Policy-basic-normal, under which normal data may be used for treatment. resource.name: IPS document that carries its consent directives
resource.description: An International Patient Summary document a Personal Health Wallet shares or an issuer issues, carrying the consent directives it is shared under, explicit or implied. Carrying them is optional (0..*); when they are carried, the Composition's Advance Directives section (LOINC 42348-3) lists them. The copy in the document is evidence for the receiver; the copy in the sharer's Consent Registry is the one enforced.

resource.name: Kinds of explicit consent (HL7 ActConsentDirective)
resource.description: The HL7 v3 ActConsentDirective codes for consent the holder gives by their own act: opt-in, opt-in with restrictions, opt-out, opt-out with exceptions. Each code's definition is HL7's (terminology.hl7.org, CodeSystem v3-ActCode).

resource.name: Kinds of implied consent (HL7 ActConsentDirective)
resource.description: The HL7 v3 ActConsentDirective codes for consent presumed from the holder's behaviour: implied consent, implied consent with opportunity to dissent, and notice of privacy practices. Each code's definition is HL7's (terminology.hl7.org, CodeSystem v3-ActCode).

resource.name: Lina's confirmation on her wallet (fictional)
resource.description: The evidence of Lina's explicit consent: the confirmation her wallet recorded when she agreed to the consent text shown to her (process L).

resource.name: Lina's explicit consent: share her summary for care abroad
resource.description: Lina agreed on her wallet that health workers abroad may read her patient summary to treat her, from 1 to 30 June 2026: an opt-in (HL7 ActConsentDirective OPTIN) that adds this permission to the opt-in default, the IHE PCF implicit policy Policy-deny. Her wallet confirmation is the evidence. The example trust domain publishes no consent codes, so there is no policyRule.

resource.name: Lina's home health information exchange (fictional): VHL Sharer and Consent Registry custodian
Lina's patient summary, shared with its consent directives (explicit and implied)
resource.description: An IPS document from Lina's wallet that carries the two consent directives it is shared under: her explicit consent and the trust domain's implied default. The Advance Directives section lists both. The copies here are evidence for the receiver; the home HIE enforces the copies in its Consent Registry.

resource.name: Ministry M (data provider)
resource.description: Ministry M, the data provider: the ODRL `assigner` of the example data sharing agreement.

resource.name: Origin country HIE (fictional): Sharer and Consent Registry custodian
PHW Consent
resource.description: A privacy consent directive held for, and shown to, the holder of a Personal Health Wallet: an IHE PCF 1.1.0 Intermediate Consent whose policy is set by a trust domain. Either explicit (PHWExplicitConsent) or implied (PHWImpliedConsent). Trust-anchor neutral: GDHCN is one possible trust anchor among others.

resource.name: PHW Explicit Consent
resource.description: A consent the holder gave by their own act: on the wallet, or on a form a health worker recorded (process L). Categorized with an HL7 ActConsentDirective code (OPTIN, OPTINR, OPTOUT or OPTOUTE). The act is the evidence (source[x]). When the trust domain publishes consent codes, policyRule names the code and the version of its text the holder was shown; otherwise policy.uri names the IHE PCF implicit policy the consent changes.

resource.name: PHW Implied Consent
resource.description: A consent the holder did not give by any act: categorized with an HL7 ActConsentDirective code (IMPLIED, IMPLIEDD or NOPP); the trust domain's default policy applies, normally an IHE PCF implicit policy (Volume 1 §1:53.2.1). Consent.policy names it, and the domain's published policy is the evidence (sourceAttachment). Carried in a document so that a receiver can see which policy the data was shared under.

resource.name: Pilgrim consent: the host Ministry of Health may use the IPS for care during Hajj
resource.description: The second of the pilgrim's two Hajj consents (CONSENT-KSA, host use). Permit, to the host Ministry of Health as information recipient, for treatment, during the example Hajj period and its follow-up. It binds the host Ministry of Health after receipt.

resource.name: Pilgrim consent: the origin HIE may release the IPS to the host Ministry of Health
resource.description: The first of the pilgrim's two Hajj consents (CONSENT-MYS, origin release). Permit, to the host Ministry of Health as information recipient, for treatment, during the example Hajj period. The origin HIE enforces it from its own Consent Registry.

resource.name: SelectiveDisclosure
resource.description:
Guidance that a document signing service with selective disclosure support (e.g. SD-JWT) should perform a selective disclosure of the content of the containing node of the extension in the JSON representation of the FHIR instance.

The code value should be from a code system containing appropriate disclosure statements for the use case.  The disclosure statement should describe the content that is to be disclosed at that node.  For example a code such as 'disclose-date-of-birth' or 'disclose-vaccine-history'.
